title: Fetch all customers with cursor pagination

conversation.text: Manual workflow: fetch ALL customers from https://api.example.com/v1/customers. The API returns { data: [...customers], next_cursor } and accepts ?cursor=<next_cursor>; keep fetching until next_cursor is null. Then POST the total number of customers to https://reports.example.com/api/customers/count as JSON field total.

description: HTTP Request pagination nests mode, parameter updates and a stop condition under options.pagination. Grades cursor pagination that stops on a null cursor.

executionScenarios.name: all-pages-fetched-once
executionScenarios.description: HTTP Request pagination nests mode, parameter updates and a stop condition under options.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: GET https://api.example.com/v1/customers with no cursor returns { "data": [{ "id": 1 }, { "id": 2 }], "next_cursor": "c2" }. With cursor=c2 it returns { "data": [{ "id": 3 }, { "id": 4 }], "next_cursor": "c3" }. With cursor=c3 it returns { "data": [{ "id": 5 }], "next_cursor": null }. Any other cursor returns 400. The count endpoint returns 200 { "ok": true }.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run fetches exactly three pages (no cursor, cursor=c2, cursor=c3), stops after next_cursor is null, and POSTs total 5. Fetching only the first page, looping past the last page, or posting a total other than 5 FAILS.

outcomeExpectations: The HTTP Request node uses built-in pagination that sets the cursor query parameter from the previous response's next_cursor and stops when next_cursor is null or missing.
